recipes.name: Tim Perry's Soup (Creamy Curry Cauliflower and Broccoli Soup)

steps.text: In a stockpot, combine chicken broth, onion, cauliflower, and broccoli. Bring to a boil and reduce heat to low. Continue to simmer until vegetables are tender. Season with curry powder, chicken bouillon, salt, and pepper.
In a bowl, combine flour and 1/2 cup of the milk. Whisk briskly until there are no lumps. Add mixture to soup, stirring continuously as soup thickens. Stir in Cheddar cheese until completely melted.

raw_recipe.headline: Tim Perry's Soup (Creamy Curry Cauliflower and Broccoli Soup)
raw_recipe.description: A simple curry soup that will not disappoint neither with its flavor, nor with its simplicity of preparation. Broccoli and cauliflower serve as the main components of this one-pot wonder. Serve with crusty bread and butter.
raw_recipe.name: Tim Perry's Soup (Creamy Curry Cauliflower and Broccoli Soup)

review.reviewBody: Loved this....although I made some changes....I sauteed the onion, 2 cloves of minced garlic, and some baby carrots in some evoo. Then I added 2 bunches of broccoli and a large head of cauliflower washed and cut into small pieces, added pepper, crushed thyme and a sprinkle of cayenne(didn't have any curry). I let that cook for about 5-7 minutes, then added the chicken broth(low sodium) and added an extra cup of water with a chicken boullion packet. Let that cook until the veggies were tender and then I whipped it through my food processor making sure I left some chunks for texture. Added that back to the pot, mixed 1% milk with the flour, let that thicken, adjusted the seasonings, and added 1 pk of shredded cheddar and the kernels of 1 leftover corn on the cob shaved off. (It was like I cleaned out the fridge!) What a fabulous soup!!! Nice and thick and rich with so many veggies.....even my 1 year old loved it....will make again and keep in my rotation for the fall/winter!!

I doubled this recipe and made it more Keto friendly and I must say it was delicious! I skipped the milk and flour and used about 1/2 cup of heavy cream (1/4 cup for the recipe as listed), I added 1/2 tsp of minced garlic and I must have missed the boullion cube listed in the recipe since I didn't add it and would have, had I seen it. I honestly didn't miss it and I always think soups need boullion. This was awesome. I ended up making this in my instapot pressure cooker on the soup setting and blending it once it cooled over night. (the blending made it sooooo creamy compared to before) Soooo good. I would make this again and again. The curry is such a good flavour in this.

This was really good! I didn't use the bouillon cubes (because I didn't have or thought it was needed) and I added some carrots because i had some. I used an immersion blender to blend coarsely but still left some pieces of the veg. I used vegetarian broth (unsalted) and salted/peppered to taste. This was so tasty. I will definitely make again.

Really enjoyed this soup! I didn’t realize I forgot cauliflower so I just used broccoli and added some carrots. I also added a couple of garlic cloves. I sautéed the garlic and onion in olive oil then added the grated carrots and broccoli for a few minutes. Then added to the pot of broth and continued following the recipe from there. Once finished I used an immersion blender to blend it smooth. Overall, very tasty and easy. Would make again!

I added 2 carrots which I sautéed with onions in 1/4 cup of butter before adding the cauliflower and brocoli. I blended everything together at the end and didn’t need the flour cause it was thick already. Served it with bacon on top!

Great recipe! I just added more vegetables. Sautéed the onions in butter with two chopped carrots, two stalks of celery and one leek. Doubled the chicken stock and tripled the curry powder. (Had a big head of cauliflower and broccoli.) Also doubled the flour-water mixture but not the cheese. Used extra sharp Cheddar and Gruyere, about three parts to one. With all that stock, I left out the bouillon granules. A couple pulses with the immersion blender and it was silky, curry happiness in a bowl.

This was very good. I sautéed the broccoli, cauliflower, onions and chopped garlic with 1/2 stick of butter. After adding the broth, I cooked it on low for about 15-20 minutes. I also added cayenne pepper. I used an immersion blender and kept some chunks purposefully. I did not use the milk, flower or bullion granules. I did add about a half teaspoon of salt. Thanks for posting

Yummy, COMFORT SOUP! Family loved it! I "tweaked" the recipe because I enjoy caramelized onions and garlic, so I sautéed the onion, garlic, and for color, added baby carrots together in EVOO, then added a small splash of white wine and teaspoon ea of cumin, and coriander (cuz I'm not yet fond of curry). Then, I followed all that up in a pot with the rest of the ingredients, and allowed it to simmer until the broccoli and cauliflower were tender. Toasted Garlic NAAN Bread was served on the side.

I made this exactly as written, and it was a huge hit. I wasn't a fan of the texture, though, so the next time I pureed it with a stick blender. The result was fantastic: creamy, rich, and with the unique curry flavor. Definitely a keeper.

Pretty tasty. I added minced garlic and fresh grated ginger and sauteed them with the onion and curry powder in a couple tablespoons of butter first. Then added in the broc/cauliflower and stock. Once cooked I blended for a smoother texture before adding in the milk and cheese. Will make again!

I have made this soup several times now. The first time I made it as is and the kids loved the cheesyness of it...but hubby and I felt it could have used some more flavor. Since that first time I have been sauteing the onions with some garlic and diced up carrots and celery. I add 2 tsp curry powder and a tsp of garam masala to the mixture and stir in together. Then add the broth and broccoli and cauliflower. I also like to blend my soup with the immersion blender...so easy! Once blended, I find that the soup is thick enough and does not need flour to thicken it. I have used milk, cream, and evaporated milk all with great success. For a nice change I like to use coconut milk...it is really yummy. I also prefer to put the cheese on the table and let everyone serve their own amount to suit their own tastes. Overall this recipe is good as is, but for our own personal tastes I would like to add more to it! Thank you for sharing a recipe that can be tweaked to suit everyone's tastes!!

This might be a better recipe if I had a different cheddar cheese and put less flour in the recipe. I also will completely blend the vegetables instead of leaving it chunky next time. I will rerate it after I give it another try.

The kids don’t like Broccolis/Cauliflour! So subbed some carots, diced, plus navybeans. Started cooking them, following all directions from the recipe but then realized this recipe calls for Curry spice!-which I don’t have!! I think recipes should really try to avoid using inaccesible spice mixes that most ppl don’t have! Thats what i took off the one star for. added in some Sweet Chili Sauc to sub for the curry spice, and then proceeded to add the Oat Milk!. Overall a great meal, the family loved it—Highly recommend this soup!!
I thought it was very yummy and will definitely make again. Added about 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric to make it even healthier .

Made this as close as possible to the directions but just a slightly larger batch. I usually roast my cauliflower for soups and had a little hesitation just using raw cauliflower, but this turned out great. My wife doesn't care for broccoli, cauliflower, or curry, so I get t freeze some of this and have it all to myself.
Yummy
Absolutely awesome! I added the carrot and celery that someone else recommended but otherwise was true to the recipe and it was great. Served with a slice of homemade bread. With make again.
I didn't have curry so I used cayenne as another user suggested. I can't wait to have it again tomorrow as we all know things taste better the second day.
Pretty good will make this again, super easy. I used heavy cream to make it richer but that is the only change I made.
This was a very good tasting soap. I add 2 cans of Campbell soup to replace the broth
